name: Note
text: Per shot: shot ID (e.g. SH010), plate source, required work (roto/paint/CG/comp), complexity tier (easy/medium/hard), and estimated hours. Bid the HARDEST shot in a sequence first — it sets your real hourly rate, everything else is comparison.

name: Note
text: Columns: Not Started / WIP / Internal Review / Client Review / Approved / Final. Move a shot only after the actual gate is passed, not "probably fine" — a shot silently sitting at 90% forever is the most common freelance-pipeline failure.

name: Note
text: Rough blocking, camera moves, and timing from the animatic or storyboard. This is the single source of truth for what a shot needs to ACCOMPLISH before final work starts — comping to a moving target wastes more hours than any technical mistake.

name: Note
text: Camera solve quality per shot (solve error in pixels — under 1px is good), lens distortion data, ground-plane/scale reference from set (a tracking marker, a known object size), and any witness-cam footage.

name: Note
text: Build ONE template comp per shot type (green-screen interview, CG-over-plate, sky replacement) with your standard keying rig, grain-match node group, and holdout setup already wired. Screenshot or link to it here — copy-pasting a working template beats rebuilding logic per shot.

name: Note
text: Dated, versioned: "v1, 2026-03-04 — director wants the explosion bigger and warmer." Never overwrite old feedback — when a client asks to revert a change three rounds later, this log is the only way to know what "before" actually looked like.

name: Note
text: 3D models, textures, or stock elements (explosions, sparks, smoke sims) sourced for this job, with license/usage terms noted next to each — a client asking "can we reuse this in the sequel" needs an answer you actually have on file.

name: Note
text: Resolution, frame rate, color space (Rec.709 vs. a client-supplied LUT), codec (ProRes 422 HQ is the safe default for review, H.264 for quick client previews), and the exact file-naming convention the client asked for — get this in writing before final render, not after.
